title: "Configuration"

# Configuration {#sec-configuration}

All settings register with `CBA_fnc_addSetting` and appear in the CBA Settings menu under the **AEE** categories. Values marked *global* must match across all clients.

## AEE Armour → Armour

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_armour_armourEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | armour | Apply the STANAG 4569-aligned vehicle armour ladder (issue #126) |

## AEE Armour → Penetration

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_armour_penetrationGate` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | armour | Scale vehicle damage by the round's real RHA penetration vs the STANAG protection class - a rifle cannot shred an IFV |

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |

## AEE Debug → Diagnostics

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_diagnostics_consistencyCheck` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | diagnostics | Read the published producer variables and warn when two modules disagree. Read-only and deterministic, so it runs on every machine. Default on. UNSOURCED that a cross-module disagreement is always a fault. |
| `aee_diagnostics_consistencyInterval` | SLIDER | `10` | yes | diagnostics | Seconds between consistency samples, range 1 to 60. Default 10. The monitor runs in a per-frame handler and throttles itself to this interval. UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_diagnostics_consistencyStrict` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | diagnostics | Also report an invariant that passes with a drift inside its tolerance and a full comparison. A no-data or out-of-scope row makes no comparison, so it is not reported. Reported at INFO, never a warning. Default off. UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_diagnostics_diagnostic` | CHECKBOX | `false` | no | diagnostics | Enable verbose diagnostic logging (diag_log) for environment state changes |
| `aee_diagnostics_logDebug` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | diagnostics | Log DEBUG and TRACE lines to the RPT. Values, not narration: each line carries the real inputs the code used. Off by default. |

## AEE Debug → Perception

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_vision_perceptionHud` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | vision | Show the one-line perception state on screen while the monitor runs. The overlay is a debug surface, so it ships off. No unit. |
| `aee_vision_perceptionInterval` | SLIDER | `0.5` | yes | vision | Minimum seconds between perception samples, range 0.1 to 2.0. The monitor runs in a per-frame handler at 0.5 s, so the effective floor is 0.5 s. Default 0.5. UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_vision_perceptionMonitor` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | vision | Publish and log the reconstructed player view state each tick. The monitor reads state other modules already publish and writes the aee_optics_perception variables; it reads no pixels. Default on. The sample cadence is the perception interval. UNSOURCED that a 0.5 s sample is the right cadence. |

## AEE Experimental → Fusion

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_thermal_fusionAlwaysOn` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | thermal | Render the thermal fusion overlay over any NVG, even without a thermal-capable headset. |
| `aee_thermal_fusionFovFrame` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Draw a thin rectangular border at the thermal channel's half-angle, so the operator can see where the fused image is actually bounded. It is a HUD aid and not optics: no mask and no tube geometry, and it draws nothing for a non-fusion device. |
| `aee_thermal_fusionOutline` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Draw the outline of each hot target the thermal state already tracks, on a transparent overlay that the NVG does not filter. It draws nothing when fusion is off or the fitted headset is not fusion capable. |
| `aee_thermal_fusionSolidFill` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | thermal | Paint each hot body inside the thermal channel one solid bright colour, the flat block a real thermal display shows. This mode replaces the graded emissive ladder while it is on, so a body is never painted by both. Turn it off for the graded look. |

## AEE Experimental → Vision

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_vision_visionAdaptationDegree` | SLIDER | `1.0` | yes | vision | Degree of chromatic adaptation D of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. CIECAM02 defines D = F times (1 - (1/3.6) times exp((-LA - 42) / 92)); F is 0.8 for a dim surround, 0.9 average, 1.0 dark. SOURCED: CIE 159:2004. The default 1.0 is a full adaptation. |
| `aee_vision_visionMesopicDesaturation` | SLIDER | `0` | yes | vision | Maximum desaturation of the human-vision model in a scotopic scene, range 0 to 0.5. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The engine can only desaturate. The exact amplitude is UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_vision_visionPurkinjeStrength` | SLIDER | `0` | yes | vision | Strength of the Purkinje shift of the human-vision model, range 0 to 1. Default 0, so the default path ships no tint. The engine ambient is green-biased and the operator rejects the tint. Raise it in AEE Experimental to opt in to the experimental mesopic path. The hue direction is SOURCED to CIE 1951. The tint amplitude is UNSOURCED. |

## AEE Eye → Eye Adaptation

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_eye_eyeAdaptationEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | eye | AEE pins the camera aperture and owns the eye adaptation rate. Off hands the camera back to the engine. |
| `aee_eye_eyeAmbientLuxScale` | SLIDER | `1` | yes | eye | Scale on the engine ambient term, no unit. UNSOURCED: getLightingAt has no documented unit. |
| `aee_eye_eyeBlindingLuxScale` | SLIDER | `0` | yes | eye | Scale on the engine blinding term, no unit. UNSOURCED: apertureParams blinding has no documented unit. Default 0, off until tuned. |
| `aee_eye_eyeFastBlend` | SLIDER | `0.35` | yes | eye | Weight of the fast pupil branch in the adapted luminance, 0 to 1. UNSOURCED: operator-tunable. |
| `aee_eye_eyeLocalLuxScale` | SLIDER | `1` | yes | eye | Scale on the engine local term, no unit. UNSOURCED: getLightingAt has no documented unit. |
| `aee_eye_eyeMesopicHigh` | SLIDER | `5` | yes | eye | Photopic end of the mesopic band, cd/m2. TRACED: CIE 191:2010, 5 cd/m2. |
| `aee_eye_eyeMesopicLow` | SLIDER | `0.005` | yes | eye | Scotopic end of the mesopic band, cd/m2. TRACED: CIE 191:2010, 0.005 cd/m2. |
| `aee_eye_eyePupilTauConstrict` | SLIDER | `0.25` | yes | eye | Pupil constriction time constant, seconds. TRACED: Meethal 2021 Sci Rep 11:21090, 0.25 s. |
| `aee_eye_eyePupilTauDilate` | SLIDER | `0.475` | yes | eye | Pupil redilation time constant, seconds. TRACED: Meethal 2021 Sci Rep 11:21090, redilation 1.9 times the constriction. |
| `aee_eye_eyeReflectance` | SLIDER | `0.18` | yes | eye | Assumed scene reflectance for the luminance step, 0 to 1. UNSOURCED: mid-grey assumption, 0.18. |
| `aee_eye_eyeTauDarkCone` | SLIDER | `120` | yes | eye | Cone-pool dark adaptation time constant, seconds. UNSOURCED: derived to fit the cone-rod break at 5 to 8 min, Hecht, Haig and Chase 1937. |
| `aee_eye_eyeTauDarkRod` | SLIDER | `400` | yes | eye | Rod-pool dark adaptation time constant, seconds. TRACED: Rushton 1961 J Physiol 156:166, 400 s. |
| `aee_eye_eyeTauLight` | SLIDER | `2.0` | yes | eye | Light-adaptation time constant, seconds. UNSOURCED: no single published perceptual value, operator-tunable, 2.0 s. |

## AEE HUD → Displays

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_cartography_mgrsCursorReadout` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | cartography | Show the aee MGRS reference and the terrain elevation at the map cursor. The vanilla cursor tooltip is engine-side and cannot be replaced, so the aee readout is drawn adjacent to it. Default on. |
| `aee_cartography_mgrsEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | cartography | Show the grid line as a full MGRS reference (zone, latitude band, 100 km square and digits) from the aee world-to-MGRS kernel instead of the engine numeric grid. Off restores the legacy numeric grid. Default on. |
| `aee_cartography_mgrsMapGrid` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | cartography | Draw the aee MGRS grid over the engine map: the grid lines and their MGRS labels at an interval that follows the zoom. The engine grid stays numeric because the CfgWorlds Grid class formats numbers only, so the aee overlay draws the MGRS lines over it. Default on. |
| `aee_cartography_mgrsPrecision` | LIST | `10` | yes | cartography | Number of MGRS digits, one of 4, 6, 8 or 10. Four digits is 1 km, six is 100 m, eight is 10 m and ten is 1 m. The digits label the south-west corner of the square and are truncated, not rounded. Default 10. |
| `aee_cartography_mgrsPrecisionAuto` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | cartography | Scale the MGRS digit count with the world map size. On: a small world gets a six-figure reference (100 m) and a large world an eight-figure one (10 m). Off: the MGRS Precision list applies. Default on. |
| `aee_hud_hudEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | hud | Show the environment HUD over the night-vision view: heading, grid, altitude, time and the aee temperature, humidity and wind |

## AEE Mobility → Rollover

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_mobility_rolloverDynamicFactor` | SLIDER | `0.8` | yes | mobility | Fraction of the static threshold a manoeuvre reaches before the inside wheels lift. Published range 0.7 to 0.9 because body roll, tyre deflection and load transfer reduce the limit. 0.8 is the default. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | mobility | Tip a vehicle whose sustained lateral acceleration exceeds its Static Stability Factor threshold. The threshold is SSF = track width / (2 x centre-of-gravity height), corrected for ground slope (Gillespie). A single frame cannot roll a vehicle; the condition must hold. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverHoldFrames` | SLIDER | `10` | yes | mobility | Frames the lateral acceleration must stay above the threshold before the vehicle rolls. A transient spike from a kerb or a collision must not roll it. Lower values roll more readily. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverRadius` | SLIDER | `50` | yes | mobility | Distance in metres within which the rollover check runs. The candidate vehicle list is cached and refreshed every 5 seconds, so the loop does not scan the world every frame. |
| `aee_mobility_rolloverTorqueScale` | SLIDER | `0.25` | yes | mobility | Rotational impulse applied per sustained roll event, scaled by vehicle mass. The engine has no tilt command, so the roll uses addTorque at the centre of mass; the impulse must be sustained to overcome the solver. |

The force comes from a per-surface speed factor: road 1.00, field 0.40 to 0.55, woodland 0.25 to 0.40, sand 0.15 to 0.30, swamp 0.10 to 0.20. The engine has no command that caps a driven vehicle's speed, so a physical force is used, applied on the driver's machine. |

A higher value pulls the vehicle to the target speed faster. The force is applied only above the target, so a slow vehicle is never dragged to a stop. |

The estimate is modelled, not documented. It uses the vehicle box size, a cited material density, and a calibrated fill factor. The switch is off until calibration passes and a human approves the model. A sourced catalogue weight always takes precedence. The estimate never replaces a documented weight. |

Snow load adds mass with setMass, and a wet or icy surface removes grip with a force. The load comes from the modelled snow depth and the sourced snow density. ## AEE Thermal → Display

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_thermal_repaintHz` | SLIDER | `4` | yes | thermal | Thermal selections repainted per second. The engine re-uploads a procedural texture for each one, and that cost lands on the render thread where no script timer sees it. The physics still solves every pass, so the image gain and every thermal coupling are unaffected. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalBaseChannel` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | The host channel for the thermal display. Vanilla TI runs the display on the engine's own thermal channel overlaid on the vehicle's native TI. DTV disables the vehicle's native TI and draws the display over the day channel instead, the route the proven A3TI and MKK thermal mods use, so the engine's TI pass cannot fight the mod's. DTV is vehicle-only: the player must be in a vehicle optic. It is a prototype for comparison and is the only channel that does not set the ppEffectForceInNVG flag. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalDisplayMode` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | Automatic follows the scene radiance histogram (AGC). Manual uses the fixed window below, like the level and span control on a real thermography or thermal weapon sight. Local normalises each object to its own selection range: it widens that object's internal contrast, but it breaks comparison between objects because a hot and a cold object can map to the same ramp. The local gain is capped at 8 times, so a flat object is not given invented contrast. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalFPN` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Add fixed-pattern noise (static spatial mottle) over painted thermal objects - the perlinNoise detail stage real LWIR sensors show on top of the temporal FilmGrain. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalManualMaxC` | SLIDER | `120` | yes | thermal | Hot end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Set it high to keep fires and exhaust on scale. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalManualMinC` | SLIDER | `-40` | yes | thermal | Cold end of the manual display window, in degrees Celsius. Used in manual display mode and as the fallback before the scene AGC is ready. The device library publishes no span, so this window is a user setting, not a device figure. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPPEffects` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Applies the full-screen thermal effects: colour grade, black-hot inversion, sensor grain, IR-scatter blur, the ocular vignette, the rain lens film and the sensor pixelation. Turn OFF to isolate their render cost. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPalette` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | Ember interpolates the engine's own decoded thermal colours through a continuous ramp. White hot grey is the luminance form of the same ramp. The isotherm modes are the MKK thermal highlight colours as procedural two-tone ramps: a body below the display window midpoint stays cold, a body at or above it takes the mode hue (red, green, yellow, magenta or sepia). |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPixelation` | CHECKBOX | `false` | yes | thermal | Quantise the thermal display to the fitted device's vertical detector resolution, so a low-resolution sensor shows the blocks its detector actually resolves. A sensor finer than the render shows none. The figure is the device's own; the engine clamps it. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalPolarity` | LIST | `0` | yes | thermal | White hot (hot = white) is the system default (AN/PAS-13 initialises white hot). Black hot (hot = black) is a user-selectable alternative - FM 3-22.9 states polarity is user preference |
| `aee_thermal_thermalWetDistortion` | SLIDER | `0.08` | yes | thermal | Maximum lens blurriness from the rain film on the objective. The display scales it from zero by the rain and fog it already models, so a dry scene shows nothing. |

| `aee_thermal_thermalHotBloom` | SLIDER | `0.08` | yes | thermal | Hot-source bloom amplitude for the thermal view, 0 to 0.15. Thermal blooming and haloing have no authoritative source; UNSOURCED. Modelled as a DynamicBlur spike, the primitive the night-vision model uses for halo. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalImperfectionsEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | thermal | Enable the thermal sensor imperfections: non-uniformity drift, temporal noise, AGC hunt and hot-source bloom. No unit. The existing fixed-pattern noise and NETD term is reused, not duplicated. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalNucDrift` | SLIDER | `0.15` | yes | thermal | Amplitude of the thermal non-uniformity (NUC) drift, 0 to 0.3. Fixed-pattern noise drifts and NUC is refreshed (Wikipedia fixed-pattern noise; EMVA 1288). The refresh cadence is UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_thermal_thermalTemporalNoise` | SLIDER | `1` | yes | thermal | Scale on the thermal temporal sensor noise, 0 to 2. Fixed-pattern and temporal noise are real sensor noise; FPN is DSNU plus PRNU, corrected by flat-field or NUC and drifting with temperature, integration time and gain (Wikipedia fixed-pattern noise; EMVA Standard 1288). |

## AEE Vision → Image

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_vision_baseGradeAcuityEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | vision | Enable the normal-vision acuity pass, a FilmGrain effect at high sharpness and low intensity. The engine has no Sharpen effect, so this is the scriptable candidate; real scene sharpening is the video option Sharpen Filter, which a mod cannot set. No unit. UNSOURCED that FilmGrain sharpness sharpens the scene. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeBlackPoint` | SLIDER | `-0.02` | yes | vision | Black-point offset of the normal-vision grade, no unit, range -0.1 to 0.1. Negative deepens the black. Community code uses -0.01 (AsYetUntitled) and -0.35 (Liberation-RX); the exact default -0.02 is UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeBrightness` | SLIDER | `1.0` | yes | vision | Display brightness of the normal-vision grade, range 0.7 to 1.3. BIKI Post Process Effects: ColorCorrections brightness, 0 black, 1 unchanged, 2 white. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeContrast` | SLIDER | `1.15` | yes | vision | Display contrast of the normal-vision grade, range 0.8 to 1.6. The ACES tone scale is an S-shaped curve with a mid-grey log-log gamma below 1.55; the engine contrast is linear, so this is a stand-in. The exact default 1.15 is UNSOURCED. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeEnabled` | CHECKBOX | `true` | yes | vision | Enable the normal-vision base grade (contrast, brightness, black point and colour weights). It applies on normal vision only and never in a sensor mode, and it owns its own ColorCorrections, so it never fights the weather grade. No unit. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeGrain` | SLIDER | `0.006` | yes | vision | FilmGrain intensity for the acuity pass, range 0 to 0.05. BIKI FilmGrain default 0.005. The engine couples grain and sharpness, so a small amount of grain is unavoidable with the sharpening. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeSaturation` | SLIDER | `0` | yes | vision | Desaturation weight of the normal-vision grade, range 0 to 0.5. BIKI ColorCorrections colorize alpha: 0 keeps the original colour, 1 is black and white. The engine can only desaturate; it cannot oversaturate. |
| `aee_vision_baseGradeSharpness` | SLIDER | `4` | yes | vision | FilmGrain sharpness for the acuity pass, range 1 to 20. BIKI FilmGrain default 1.25. The wiki does not state what it sharpens, so that it sharpens the scene is UNSOURCED; it is a display-aesthetic compromise, not added human acuity. |

## AEE → Core

| Setting | Type | Default | Global | Addon | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_core_computeMode` | LIST | `"DETERMINISTIC"` | yes | core | Where the environment computation runs. Deterministic (default): every machine computes the same values with NO network traffic. Costs the same CPU on server and clients, and is the only mode that cannot desynchronise. Server authority: the server computes and broadcasts the shared state each tick. Lowers client CPU at the cost of roughly 0.6 MB per minute per client at an 80 player count, and it needs a full resync when a player joins mid mission. Server map facts only: the server computes the once-per-mission terrain facts and every machine keeps its own position work. A few hundred bytes once, and it removes the only startup hitch on a large map. |

## AEE FX → Exhaust plume

Per-vehicle published values.  A mission or a mod sets these on a vehicle
object.  They are not CBA settings.

| Variable | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aee_exhaustTier` | STRING | unset | Tier override, one of `land`, `heli`, `jet`, `ab`. Wins over the class selection |
| `aee_exhaustAfterburner` | BOOL | unset | A truthy value selects the afterburner tier, because no verified config key distinguishes an afterburning jet from a dry one |
| `aee_enginePowerFraction` | NUMBER | unset | Engine power fraction in 0..1. Overrides the real reader and the declared idle |
| `aee_engineRatedPowerW` | NUMBER | `150000` | Rated engine power in watts for the derived ground load. Overrides the declared default |
| `aee_exhaustGasTempC` | NUMBER | unset | Measured exhaust gas temperature in Celsius. Overrides the class row |
| `aee_exhaustPlumeM` | NUMBER | unset | Measured plume depth in metres. Overrides the class row |

The class row comes from the tier table in `fnc_applyExhaustShimmer.sqf`,
and `fnc_calculateExhaustPlume.sqf` interpolates it from the engine power
fraction.  The endpoints are declared defaults and not measurements.  When
no published value is set, the power fraction comes from the real reader,
`collectiveRTD` for a helicopter and `throttleRTD` for fixed wing, which is
gated on the advanced helicopter flight model and is unavailable when it is
off.  A land vehicle and a gated-off client use the declared idle fraction.


## AEE Optics → Intensity (historical)

The night-vision grain ceilings moved to the Night Vision addon and now
register as `aee_nightvision_nightGrainMax`, `aee_nightvision_rainGrainMax`
and `aee_nightvision_fogGrainMax`. The older names are kept here.

| `aee_optics_rainGrainMax` | SLIDER | `0.4` | optics | Rain-on-eye noise at night |
| `aee_optics_fogGrainMax` | SLIDER | `0.15` | optics | Fog haze grain added to the night grain effect |
